chapter: Return to New York, addiction, health and the NBC job
title: Quitting heroin in 1966 and the 'slow suicide' of addiction
summary: He says he was tired of waiting on connections and describes addiction as slow suicide.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: So when did you finally end it?

'66, I was tired. Like you spend most of your time waiting for the connection to show up. That's the biggest hassle in the world. You can have money and the man's never on the scene. You've got to wait and wait and wait and wait and wait, or else you get burned, you know. A burn is some flea powder, something you can't even feel, you know, and you've spent your last money for it, and where are you going to get some

more money, and you haven't felt anything. You're still sick. It's a horrible life. And a drug addict is undoubtedly the biggest fool that God created on earth, I think. From this standpoint, he doesn't know anything about medicine. All you've got to do is tell him it's heroin and it'll cook up and you can draw it up in a syringe, he'll put it in his arm. You know? And that's how all these hotshots and overdoses and things come about, you know?
But if you knew all this, and you said you argued all this to Billie, way back in the '40s, then how come you let it happen to you? Or is that an oversimplified question?

No, well I said after I seen that I wasn't going any further, like I wanted to commit suicide. Like people say it's a coward that commits suicide. I think it's a brave man that commits suicide, take his own life. Because I'm not that cowardly and I'm not that brave, you know, so I was commiting suicide the slow way, you know. I'd say, well, if I commit suicide, they will lift the record, the cabaret license off and someone will call for me and I won't be here, you know, to answer the bell, answer the phone.
Yeah. Well, it was a slow, methodical thing, you know. So I just got tired.
So your suicide didn't work out, so you
Yeah. But I've been spending the rest of the time trying to live. You know.
